prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Dallas. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?

answer_verbatim:
For a dental implant, I’d make **two types of calls**: one to a practice that can plan and place the implant surgically, and one to a **prosthodontist** (the dentist specializing in crowns, bridges, dentures, and implant restorations). The crown/teeth are just as important as the implant post.

Here are Dallas-area places worth calling first:

| Practice / clinic | Why call | Best fit |
|---|---|---|
| **Texas A&M College of Dentistry — Advanced Prosthodontics and Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery clinics, Dallas** | A strong option for a comprehensive second opinion. Their specialty clinics can coordinate the surgical implant, bone grafting if needed, and final crown/denture planning. Faculty supervision is useful for complex cases. | You want a thorough plan, have multiple missing teeth, need a second opinion, or are open to a teaching-clinic setting. It may cost less than some private offices, but usually takes more appointments and may have longer scheduling. |
| **UT Southwestern Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, Dallas** | Hospital/academic oral-surgery setting; particularly worth contacting if you have significant medical issues, take blood thinners, have diabetes, need sedation, have major bone loss, or may need grafting. | Medically complex cases, difficult extractions, bone grafting, or patients who want a hospital-affiliated surgical opinion. Ask whether they accept direct implant consultations or require a referral. |
| **Dallas Oral Surgery Associates** | A private oral-and-maxillofacial-surgery practice that can evaluate implant placement, extraction, sedation, and bone grafting. A private surgical practice is often more convenient and faster than an academic clinic. | You already have a general dentist/prosthodontist who will make the crown, or you need the surgical part handled by a specialist. Ask who will coordinate the final restoration. |
| **North Texas Center for Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery** | Another Dallas-area oral-surgery group to use as a comparison consultation, especially for implant surgery, grafting, and sedation. Getting a second surgical opinion can be valuable if you were told you need a sinus lift, extensive grafting, or an “All-on-4”-type treatment. | You want a second estimate or have a more involved surgical case. Confirm the office location most convenient to you and whether they work with your restoring dentist. |

## My practical recommendation

1. **Call Texas A&M College of Dentistry first** if your situation is complex, you want a teaching/faculty-supervised opinion, or cost matters.
2. **Call Dallas Oral Surgery Associates or North Texas Center for Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery** for a private-practice surgical consultation and a comparison estimate.
3. If you have medical conditions, need IV sedation, or were told you have substantial bone loss, **also call UT Southwestern Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery.**
4. If you do not already have a restorative dentist, ask each office:  
   **“Who will design and place my final implant crown or denture, and will that person be involved before surgery?”**

## What to ask on the phone

Use this short script:

> “I’m considering a dental implant. Do you offer a consultation that includes a CBCT/3-D scan if needed? Is the surgeon a board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgeon or is there a prosthodontist involved? Can you give me an itemized estimate for extraction, bone grafting, implant, abutment, crown, sedation, and follow-up?”

Also ask:

- Is the quote **all-inclusive**, or is the crown/abutment separate?
- Will they submit a **pre-treatment estimate** to your dental insurance?
- What implant brand/system do they use, and can another dentist service it later?
- If bone grafting is needed, is that included in the estimate?
- How long from extraction to final crown?
- Who handles complications or implant maintenance?
- For full-mouth “same-day teeth” offers: is the advertised price per arch, and does it include temporary and final teeth?

## One caution

Be skeptical of ads that lead with a very low implant price. That often covers only the implant post—not the extraction, CT scan, graft, abutment, final crown, sedation, or temporary tooth. For a fair comparison, get each office to provide the estimate in writing with every component listed.

If you tell me your Dallas ZIP code, whether this is **one tooth or several**, and whether you have insurance or a budget range, I can narrow this to the most practical 2–3 offices to call first.
